title: Heart Failure Home Teaching
brief: Create a plain-language heart failure teaching handout for a patient and family preparing for discharge.

delegate.scenario: You are preparing discharge education for a patient who has been treated for heart failure and will manage daily care at home with help from a family member. The patient and family will review the handout with you before leaving the hospital, so it needs to be practical and easy to discuss.
delegate.inputs:
Discharge teaching notes for Mr. Luis Ortega and his daughter Elena. They prefer plain English and want a simple daily routine they can keep on the refrigerator.

Diagnosis: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. He is feeling better and is going home with family support. Explain daily weights, lower-sodium eating, activity pacing, and when to call the care team or seek urgent help. Ask them to repeat back the weight plan and warning signs.

Discharge date: 06/17/2026
Follow-up: cardiology appointment 06/24/2026 at 10:30 AM; bring the weight log and medication list.

Medication list: furosemide 40 mg by mouth each morning; lisinopril 10 mg by mouth each morning; Amlodipine 5 mg by mouth each morning. Take amlodipine 10 mg every morning.

Weigh every morning after using the bathroom and before breakfast, using the same scale. Call the care team for a gain of 2 lb overnight or 5 lb in a week, worsening ankle swelling, or more shortness of breath. Seek emergency help for severe trouble breathing or chest pain.

Discharged home 06/16/2026. He can walk short distances with rest breaks. Keep sodium under 2,000 mg per day and avoid adding salt at the table.
delegate.goal: A good handout helps the patient and daughter follow the home-care plan safely and know when to contact the care team.

criteria.text: Says the handout is for the patient and family, using plain English.
Organizes the advice into practical daily actions and clear warning signs.
Keeps the supplied care instructions intact and does not add unsupported medical advice.
Asks the AI to check medication instructions against the source and flag conflicts rather than guess.
Requests a concise, refrigerator-friendly format with clear headings and bullets.
Includes a teach-back prompt for the weight plan and when to seek help.

traps.description: The medication list gives amlodipine as 5 mg each morning, while another instruction says 10 mg every morning.
evidence: Amlodipine 5 mg by mouth each morning

traps.description: The discharge date is listed as both 06/17/2026 and 06/16/2026.

delegate.exemplar: Create a concise, refrigerator-friendly discharge teaching handout for Mr. Ortega and his daughter, using plain English. Organize it with clear headings and bullets for the daily routine, food and activity guidance, and warning signs with actions to take. Use only the information in the notes; do not add medical advice. Check every medication instruction against the source and list any mismatch for the nurse to verify rather than choosing a dose. Include a teach-back prompt about the weight plan and when to seek help.
